newsitem.title: USA: AT&T up on FCC long-distance reform proposal.
newsitem.headline: AT&T up on FCC long-distance reform proposal.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission's proposal for long-distance access charge reform gave AT&T Corp's stock a boost on Thursday, pushing it up 1-1/4 to 42-3/4 by shortly after noon.
The FCC's proposal to trim the $23 billion long-distance companies pay to local service providers in access fees would benefit AT&T and other long distance providers, analysts said.
WorldCom Inc gained 7/8 to 24-7/8 and MFS Communications gained 1-1/2 to 51-3/4.
"AT&T's not looking at sudden windfall. But AT&T's moving on some hope on access charge reform," said Scott Wright, an analyst with Argus Research.
"The stock has been beaten down about all it can be this year. The big changes are behind it. I think there are enough institutions that will want to get in on an early turnaround," Wright said.
Other analysts said investors over-emphasized the FCC proposal due to the lack of other news in post-holiday trading.
AT&T topped the New York Stock Exchange's list of most active stocks. The Dow Jones industrials gained about 37 to 6559 at midday.
